0.title: make()
0.text:
The **make** method creates a new collection instance from the given items.
You may pass an array, an object, or an existing collection:

1.title: wrap()
1.text:
The **wrap** method will wrap the given value in a collection. If the given
value is already a collection, it will be returned unchanged:

2.title: unwrap()
2.text:
The **unwrap** method returns the underlying items from the given value.
If the value is a collection, the underlying array is returned. If the
value is already an array, it is returned unchanged:

3.title: empty()
3.text:
The **empty** method returns an empty collection. This is useful when you
need a typed empty collection as a starting point:

4.title: range()
4.text:
The **range** method creates a collection containing numbers within a specified range.

Works in both directions: ascending when `from < to`, descending otherwise.

5.title: times()
5.text:
The **times** method creates a new collection by invoking the given closure a specified number of times.

The callback receives 1-based indices (1, 2, 3...). Without a callback,
returns a collection of numbers 1 through N.

6.title: fromJson()
6.text: The **fromJson** method creates a collection from a JSON string:

7.title: all()
7.text: The **all** method returns the underlying array or object represented by the collection:

8.title: get()
8.text:
The **get** method returns the item at a given key. If the key does not exist,
`null` is returned. Optionally, pass a default value as the second argument.

9.title: getOrPut()
9.text:
The **getOrPut** method retrieves the value for the given key. If the key does not
exist, the default value is stored in the collection and returned.

10.title: first()
10.text:
The **first** method returns the first element in the collection that passes a given truth test.

You may also call the method with no arguments to get the first element. If the collection
is empty, the default value or undefined is returned.

11.title: last()
11.text:
The **last** method returns the last element in the collection that passes a given truth test.

You may also call the method with no arguments to get the last element. If the collection
is empty, the default value or undefined is returned.

12.title: keys()
12.text:
The **keys** method returns all of the collection's keys as a new collection.
For array-backed collections, this returns the numeric indices as strings.

13.title: values()
13.text:
The **values** method returns all of the collection's values as a new
collection with reset, sequential integer keys.

14.title: map()
14.text:
The **map** method iterates over the collection and passes each value to the given callback.
The callback is free to modify the item and return it, thus forming a new collection of
modified items.

15.title: mapWithKeys()
15.text:
The **mapWithKeys** method iterates through the collection and passes each value
to the given callback. The callback should return an associative array containing
a single key/value pair.

16.title: mapToDictionary()
16.text:
The **mapToDictionary** method runs the given callback over each item and groups
the returned values by their keys.

17.title: mapToGroups()
17.text:
The **mapToGroups** method groups the collection's items by the given callback.
The callback returns a [key, value] tuple that determines the grouping.

18.title: mapInto()
18.text:
The **mapInto** method iterates over the collection and creates a new instance
of the given class for each item, passing the item value and key to the constructor.

19.title: mapSpread()
19.text:
The **mapSpread** method iterates over the collection's items, passing each nested
item value into the given callback as separate arguments.

20.title: flatMap()
20.text: Map each item then flatten the results by one level.

21.title: filter()
21.text:
The **filter** method filters the collection using the given callback, keeping only
items that pass a given truth test. If no callback is supplied, all falsy values
(`false`, `null`, `undefined`, `0`, `''`) are removed.

22.title: reject()
22.text:
The **reject** method filters the collection using the given callback, removing
items that pass the truth test. It is the inverse of the `filter` method.

23.title: collapse()
23.text:
The **collapse** method collapses a collection of arrays into a single, flat collection.
It merges the elements of nested arrays or Collections into one level.

24.title: collapseWithKeys()
24.text:
The **collapseWithKeys** method collapses a collection of arrays into a single, flat
collection while preserving the original keys.

25.title: flatten()
25.text:
The **flatten** method flattens a multi-dimensional collection into a single dimension.
You may optionally pass a depth argument to limit how many levels deep the flattening
should go.

26.title: flip()
26.text:
The **flip** method swaps the collection's keys with their corresponding values. Values
are converted to strings since object keys must be strings.

27.title: chunk()
27.text: Split the collection into chunks of the given size.

28.title: chunkWhile()
28.text:
The **chunkWhile** method breaks the collection into multiple, smaller collections
based on the evaluation of the given callback.

29.title: split()
29.text:
The **split** method breaks a collection into the given number of groups,
distributing extra items across earlier groups to balance sizes.

30.title: splitIn()
30.text:
The **splitIn** method breaks a collection into the given number of groups,
filling non-terminal groups completely before allocating the remainder
to the final group.

31.title: slice()
31.text:
The **slice** method returns a slice of the collection starting at the
given index. You may pass a second argument to limit the size of the
returned slice.

32.title: reverse()
32.text:
The **reverse** method reverses the order of the collection's items, preserving the
original keys.

33.title: shuffle()
33.text:
The **shuffle** method randomly shuffles the items in the collection.

Uses the Fisher-Yates algorithm for unbiased shuffling.

34.title: pad()
34.text:
The **pad** method fills the array with the given value until the array reaches
the specified size. This method behaves like PHP's `array_pad` function.

To pad to the left, specify a negative size. No padding occurs if the absolute
value of the given size is less than or equal to the length of the array.

35.title: zip()
35.text:
The **zip** method merges together the values of the given array with the values
of the original collection at their corresponding index.

36.title: contains()
36.text:
The **contains** method determines whether the collection contains a given item.

Uses loose equality (`==`) to match Laravel behavior. Note that JS differs from PHP:
`0 == false`, `null == undefined`, `"" == 0`.

37.title: containsStrict()
37.text:
The **containsStrict** method determines if the collection contains a given item
using strict comparison (`===`).

38.title: doesntContain()
38.text:
The **doesntContain** method determines if the collection does not contain a given item.
This is the inverse of {@link contains}.

39.title: doesntContainStrict()
39.text:
The **doesntContainStrict** method determines if the collection does not contain
a given item using strict comparison.

40.title: diff()
40.text:
The **diff** method compares the collection against another array or collection
based on its values. This method returns the values in the original collection
that are not present in the given collection.

41.title: diffUsing()
41.text:
The **diffUsing** method compares the collection against another array or collection
using a callback for comparison. The callback should return 0 when two values are
considered equal.

42.title: diffKeys()
42.text:
The **diffKeys** method compares the collection against another array or collection
based on its keys. This method returns the key/value pairs in the original collection
that are not present in the given collection.

43.title: diffKeysUsing()
43.text:
The **diffKeysUsing** method compares the collection against another array or collection
based on its keys using a callback. The callback should return 0 when two keys are
considered equal.

44.title: diffAssoc()
44.text:
The **diffAssoc** method compares the collection against another array or collection
based on its keys and values. This method returns the key/value pairs in the original
collection that are not present in the given collection.

45.title: diffAssocUsing()
45.text:
The **diffAssocUsing** method compares the collection against another array or collection
based on its keys and values, using a callback for key comparison. The callback should
return 0 when two keys are considered equal.

46.title: intersect()
46.text:
The **intersect** method removes any values from the original collection that are not
present in the given array or collection.

47.title: intersectUsing()
47.text:
The **intersectUsing** method removes values not present in the given array or collection,
using a callback for comparison. The callback should return 0 when two values are
considered equal.

48.title: intersectAssoc()
48.text:
The **intersectAssoc** method compares the collection against another array or collection,
returning key/value pairs that are present in both. Unlike `intersect`, this method
considers both keys and values when determining matches.

49.title: intersectAssocUsing()
49.text:
The **intersectAssocUsing** method compares the collection against another array or collection
based on both keys and values, using a callback for key comparison. The callback should
return 0 when two keys are considered equal.

50.title: intersectByKeys()
50.text:
The **intersectByKeys** method removes any keys from the original collection that are
not present in the given array or collection.

51.title: duplicates()
51.text: The **duplicates** method retrieves and returns duplicate values from the collection.

52.title: duplicatesStrict()
52.text:
The **duplicatesStrict** method retrieves duplicate values from the collection using strict
equality (`===`). Unlike `duplicates`, this method distinguishes between values like `1` and `'1'`.

53.title: median()
53.text:
The **median** method returns the median value of a given key.
The median is the middle value when all values are sorted in order.
For collections with an even number of items, it returns the average of the two middle values.

54.title: mode()
54.text:
The **mode** method returns the mode value of a given key.
The mode is the value that appears most often. If multiple values appear
with the same frequency, all of them are returned.

55.title: count()
55.text: The **count** method returns the total number of items in the collection.

56.title: countBy()
56.text:
The **countBy** method counts the occurrences of values in the collection.
By default it counts by the value itself, but you can pass a callback or
property key to count by a derived grouping key.

57.title: sum()
57.text: Sum all items, or a specific key/callback result.

58.title: avg()
58.text: The **avg** method returns the average value of a given key.

59.title: average()
59.text:
The **average** method returns the average value of a given key.
This is an alias for the {@link avg} method.

60.title: min()
60.text: The **min** method returns the minimum value of a given key.

61.title: max()
61.text: The **max** method returns the maximum value of a given key.

62.title: percentage()
62.text:
The **percentage** method may be used to quickly determine the percentage of
items in the collection that pass a given truth test.

63.title: merge()
63.text:
The **merge** method merges the given array or collection with the original collection.
If a string key in the given items matches a string key in the original collection,
the given item's value will overwrite the value in the original collection.

64.title: mergeRecursive()
64.text:
The **mergeRecursive** method merges the given array or collection recursively with
the original collection. If a string key in the given items matches a string key
in the original collection, then the values for these keys are merged together
into an array, and this is done recursively.

65.title: union()
65.text:
The **union** method adds the given array to the collection. If the given array
contains keys that are already in the original collection, the original
collection's values will be preferred.

66.title: combine()
66.text:
The **combine** method combines the values of the collection, as keys, with the
values of another array or collection.

67.title: crossJoin()
67.text:
The **crossJoin** method cross joins the collection's values among the given
arrays or collections, returning a Cartesian product with all possible permutations.

68.title: concat()
68.text:
The **concat** method appends the given array or collection's values onto the end
of another collection. Unlike `merge`, this method does not consider keys and
simply appends all values to the end.

69.title: put()
69.text:
The **put** method sets the given key and value in the collection.
This method modifies the collection in place.

70.title: pull()
70.text:
The **pull** method removes and returns an item from the collection by its key.
This method modifies the collection in place.

71.title: push()
71.text:
The **push** method appends an item to the end of the collection.
This method modifies the collection in place.

72.title: prepend()
72.text:
The **prepend** method adds an item to the beginning of the collection.
This method modifies the collection in place.

73.title: unshift()
73.text: The **unshift** method adds one or more items to the beginning of the collection.

74.title: pop()
74.text:
The **pop** method removes and returns the last item from the collection.
This method modifies the collection in place.

75.title: shift()
75.text:
The **shift** method removes and returns the first item from the collection.
This method modifies the collection in place.

76.title: add()
76.text:
The **add** method appends an item to the end of the collection.
This is an alias for {@link push}.

77.title: forget()
77.text:
The **forget** method removes an item from the collection by its key.
This method modifies the collection in place. Unlike `except`, this method
modifies the collection directly.

78.title: except()
78.text: The **except** method returns all items in the collection except for those with the specified keys.

79.title: only()
79.text: The **only** method returns the items in the collection with the specified keys.

80.title: select()
80.text:
The **select** method selects the given keys from the collection, similar to
an SQL SELECT statement.

81.title: has()
81.text:
The **has** method determines if one or more keys exist in the collection.
When checking multiple keys, all must exist for the method to return true.

82.title: hasAny()
82.text:
The **hasAny** method determines if any of the given keys exist in the collection.
Returns true if at least one key exists.

83.title: groupBy()
83.text: Group items by a key or callback result.

84.title: keyBy()
84.text:
Key the collection by a field or callback result.

If multiple items have the same key, only the last one is kept.

85.title: partition()
85.text: Split the collection into two groups: items passing the test and items failing.

86.title: search()
86.text:
The **search** method searches the collection for the given value and returns
its key if found. If the item is not found, `false` is returned.

87.title: sort()
87.text:
The **sort** method sorts the collection. The sorted collection keeps the original
array keys for associative collections, but resets numeric keys for array collections.

88.title: sortDesc()
88.text: The **sortDesc** method sorts the collection in descending order.

89.title: sortBy()
89.text:
The **sortBy** method sorts the collection by the given key.

The sorted collection keeps the original array keys, so in the following example
we will use the `values` method to reset the keys to consecutively numbered indexes.

90.title: sortByDesc()
90.text:
The **sortByDesc** method sorts the collection in the opposite order as the `sortBy` method.

This method has the same signature as `sortBy`, but will sort in descending order.

91.title: sortKeys()
91.text: The **sortKeys** method sorts the collection by its keys.

92.title: sortKeysDesc()
92.text: The **sortKeysDesc** method sorts the collection by its keys in descending order.

93.title: sortKeysUsing()
93.text:
The **sortKeysUsing** method sorts the collection by its keys using a callback.
The callback should return a negative, zero, or positive integer based on comparison.

94.title: skip()
94.text: The **skip** method returns a new collection without the first N items.

95.title: skipUntil()
95.text:
The **skipUntil** method skips items until the given callback returns true,
then returns the remaining items.

96.title: skipWhile()
96.text:
The **skipWhile** method skips items while the given callback returns true,
then returns the remaining items.

97.title: take()
97.text:
The **take** method returns a new collection with the specified number of
items. You may pass a negative integer to take that many items from the
end of the collection.

98.title: takeUntil()
98.text: The **takeUntil** method returns items until the given callback returns true.

99.title: takeWhile()
99.text:
The **takeWhile** method returns items while the given callback returns true.
Once the callback returns false, it stops.

100.title: implode()
100.text:
The **implode** method joins items in a collection.

Its arguments depend on the type of items in the collection. If the collection contains
arrays or objects, pass the key of the attribute you wish to join, and the "glue" string.
For simple values, pass just the glue string.

101.title: join()
101.text:
The **join** method joins the collection's values with a string.

Using its second argument, you may also specify how the final element should be appended,
which is useful for natural-language formatting like "and" or "or".

102.title: toString()
102.text:
The **toString** method returns the collection as a string representation.
For arrays, items are joined with commas. For objects, returns JSON.

103.title: isEmpty()
103.text: The **isEmpty** method returns `true` if the collection is empty; otherwise, `false` is returned.

104.title: isNotEmpty()
104.text: The **isNotEmpty** method returns `true` if the collection is not empty; otherwise, `false` is returned.

105.title: containsOneItem()
105.text: The **containsOneItem** method returns `true` if the collection contains exactly one item.

106.title: hasMany()
106.text:
The **hasMany** method determines if multiple items exist in the collection
that match the given criteria.

107.title: hasSole()
107.text:
The **hasSole** method determines if exactly one item exists in the collection
that matches the given criteria.

108.title: sole()
108.text:
The **sole** method returns the first element in the collection that passes
a given truth test, but only if exactly one element matches. If no elements
match or more than one element matches, an exception is thrown.

109.title: firstOrFail()
109.text:
The **firstOrFail** method returns the first element in the collection, or throws
an exception if the collection is empty.

110.title: pluck()
110.text: Extract values at a given path from each item.

111.title: transform()
111.text:
The **transform** method iterates over the collection and calls the given callback
with each item in the collection. The items in the collection will be replaced
by the values returned by the callback. Unlike `map`, this method modifies the
collection in place.

112.title: nth()
112.text: The **nth** method returns every n-th element of the collection.

113.title: random()
113.text: The **random** method returns a random item from the collection.

114.title: sliding()
114.text:
The **sliding** method returns a new collection of chunks representing a
"sliding window" view of the items in the collection.

115.title: multiply()
115.text: The **multiply** method creates multiple copies of all items in the collection.

116.title: replace()
116.text:
The **replace** method replaces items in the collection by key. Existing keys will be
overwritten with the new values. This is useful for merging settings or configurations
where you want to ensure certain keys are updated.

117.title: replaceRecursive()
117.text:
The **replaceRecursive** method works like `replace`, but it will recurse into
nested objects and apply the same replacement process to the inner values.

118.title: splice()
118.text:
The **splice** method removes and returns a slice of items starting at the
specified index. You may pass a second argument to limit the size of the
removed slice, and a third argument containing replacement items.
This method modifies the original collection.

119.title: dot()
119.text:
The **dot** method flattens a multi-dimensional collection into a single level
collection that uses "dot" notation to indicate depth. This is useful for
working with nested configuration or form data.

120.title: undot()
120.text:
The **undot** method expands a single-level collection that uses "dot" notation
into a multi-dimensional collection. This is the inverse of the `dot` method.

121.title: unique()
121.text:
The **unique** method returns all of the unique items in the collection.

When dealing with nested objects, you may specify a key used to determine uniqueness.

122.title: uniqueStrict()
122.text:
The **uniqueStrict** method has the same signature as the `unique` method
but uses strict comparison (`===`) to filter unique values.

123.title: where()
123.text:
The **where** method filters the collection by a given key/value pair.

The method uses "loose" comparisons when checking item values, meaning
a string with an integer value will be considered equal to an integer
of the same value. Use the `whereStrict` method for strict comparisons.

You may optionally pass a comparison operator as the second argument.
Supported operators: `=`, `==`, `!=`, `<>`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`.

124.title: whereStrict()
124.text:
The **whereStrict** method filters the collection by a given key/value pair using strict
comparison (`===`). Unlike `where`, this method distinguishes between values like `1` and `'1'`.

125.title: whereIn()
125.text: The **whereIn** method filters the collection by a given key/value contained within the given array.

126.title: whereInStrict()
126.text: The **whereInStrict** method filters the collection using strict comparison.

127.title: whereNotIn()
127.text: The **whereNotIn** method filters the collection by a given key/value not contained within the given array.

128.title: whereNotInStrict()
128.text: The **whereNotInStrict** method filters the collection using strict comparison.

129.title: whereBetween()
129.text:
The **whereBetween** method filters the collection by determining if a specified
item value is within a given range (inclusive).

130.title: whereNotBetween()
130.text:
The **whereNotBetween** method filters the collection by determining if a specified item value
is outside of a given range.

131.title: whereNull()
131.text:
The **whereNull** method filters the collection by determining if a specified
item value is null or undefined.

132.title: whereNotNull()
132.text:
The **whereNotNull** method filters the collection by determining if a specified
item value is not null and not undefined.

133.title: whereInstanceOf()
133.text:
The **whereInstanceOf** method filters the collection by a given class type,
keeping only items that are instances of the specified class.

134.title: firstWhere()
134.text:
The **firstWhere** method returns the first element in the collection with the
given key/value pair.

135.title: each()
135.text:
The **each** method iterates over the items in the collection and passes each item to a closure.

If you would like to stop iterating through the items, you may return false from your closure.

136.title: eachSpread()
136.text:
The **eachSpread** method iterates over the collection's items, passing each nested
item value into the given callback as separate arguments.

137.title: reduce()
137.text:
The **reduce** method reduces the collection to a single value, passing the result of each
iteration into the subsequent iteration.

The value for the accumulator on the first iteration is the initial value; on subsequent
iterations, it is the value returned by the previous callback.

138.title: reduceSpread()
138.text: The **reduceSpread** method reduces the collection to multiple values using spread arguments.

139.title: reduceWithKeys()
139.text:
The **reduceWithKeys** method reduces the collection with access to both value and key.

This method works identically to `reduce` since the key is always provided as the third
argument. It exists for API compatibility with Laravel.

140.title: reduceInto()
140.text:
The **reduceInto** method reduces the collection into an existing object, mutating it.

Unlike `reduce`, the callback does not return a value. Instead, it modifies the carry
object directly. The same object is returned at the end.

141.title: every()
141.text:
The **every** method verifies that all elements of the collection pass a given truth test.

Returns `true` if the callback returns truthy for every item. If the collection is
empty, **every** returns `true` (vacuous truth).

142.title: some()
142.text:
The **some** method is an alias for the `contains` method.

It determines whether the collection contains any items that pass the given truth test.
This method is useful for developers coming from JavaScript's Array.some() convention.

143.title: toArray()
143.text:
The **toArray** method converts the collection into a plain array. For
associative collections, only the values are returned:

144.title: toJson()
144.text: The **toJson** method converts the collection into a JSON serialized string.

145.title: toPrettyJson()
145.text:
The **toPrettyJson** method converts the collection into a formatted JSON string
with indentation for readability.

146.title: collect()
146.text:
The **collect** method returns a new Collection instance with the current items.
This is useful when you want to break the chain and get a fresh collection,
or convert a subclass back to a base Collection.

147.title: toBase()
147.text:
The **toBase** method returns a base Collection instance from the current collection.
This is useful when working with collection subclasses and you need to ensure
you have a standard Collection instance.

148.title: pipe()
148.text:
The **pipe** method passes the collection to the given closure and returns the result
of the executed closure. This is useful for wrapping the collection in custom logic
or breaking out of the method chain when needed.

149.title: pipeInto()
149.text:
The **pipeInto** method creates a new instance of the given class and passes the
collection into the constructor. This is useful for wrapping the collection in
domain-specific objects or adapters.

150.title: pipeThrough()
150.text:
The **pipeThrough** method passes the collection through a series of callbacks and
returns the final result. Each callback receives the result of the previous callback,
creating a pipeline of transformations.

151.title: tap()
151.text:
Pass the collection to the given callback and return it unchanged.

Useful for debugging or side effects mid-chain.

152.title: dump()
152.text:
The **dump** method outputs the collection's items to the console and returns the
collection, allowing you to inspect the contents at any point in a method chain
without interrupting the flow.

153.title: dd()
153.text:
The **dd** method outputs the collection's items to the console and then throws
an error to halt script execution. This is useful for debugging when you want
to inspect the collection and stop processing. The name comes from "dump and die."

154.title: forPage()
154.text:
The **forPage** method returns a new collection containing the items that
would be present on a given page number.

155.title: value()
155.text: The **value** method retrieves a given value from the first element of the collection.

156.title: when()
156.text:
The **when** method executes the given callback when the first argument evaluates to true.
The collection instance and the resolved value are passed to the closure.
An optional second callback is executed when the condition is falsy.

157.title: unless()
157.text:
The **unless** method executes the given callback when the first argument evaluates to false.
This is the inverse of the `when` method. An optional second callback is executed when
the condition is truthy.

158.title: whenEmpty()
158.text:
The **whenEmpty** method executes the given callback when the collection is empty.
An optional second callback is executed when the collection is not empty.

159.title: whenNotEmpty()
159.text:
The **whenNotEmpty** method executes the given callback when the collection is not empty.
An optional second callback is executed when the collection is empty.

160.title: unlessEmpty()
160.text:
The **unlessEmpty** method executes the given callback when the collection is not empty.
This is an alias for {@link whenNotEmpty}.

161.title: unlessNotEmpty()
161.text:
The **unlessNotEmpty** method executes the given callback when the collection is empty.
This is an alias for {@link whenEmpty}.

162.title: offsetExists()
162.text:
The **offsetExists** method determines if a key exists at the given offset.

This method implements the ArrayAccess interface pattern, allowing bracket-style
key existence checks. It is used internally for array-like access.

163.title: offsetGet()
163.text:
The **offsetGet** method returns the value at a given offset.

Part of the ArrayAccess interface for bracket-style access. Unlike
`get()`, this method does not support default values and returns
`undefined` for missing keys.

164.title: offsetSet()
164.text:
The **offsetSet** method sets the value at a given offset.

Part of the ArrayAccess interface for bracket-style assignment. If the key is `null`,
the value is appended to the collection (like `push`). This method modifies the
collection in place.

165.title: offsetUnset()
165.text:
The **offsetUnset** method removes the value at a given offset.

Part of the ArrayAccess interface for bracket-style deletion. This method modifies
the collection in place. For arrays, this does not re-index the remaining items.

166.title: with()
166.text:
The **with** method pairs the collection with a related collection, creating a
WithCollection that allows ORM-style operations where each primary item can be
processed alongside filtered related items.

167.title: lazy()
167.text:
The **lazy** method returns a new LazyCollection instance from the underlying items.

This is particularly useful when you need to perform transformations on a large collection
and want to defer processing until the items are actually needed. LazyCollection only
processes items as they're consumed, which can significantly reduce memory usage and
improve performance for large datasets.

168.title: lazyFirst()
168.text:
Find the first item matching a predicate without creating LazyCollection.
Faster than `.lazy().first()` for simple lookups.

169.title: after()
169.text:
The **after** method returns the item after the given item.
Returns null if the item is not found or is the last item.

170.title: before()
170.text:
The **before** method returns the item before the given item.
Returns null if the item is not found or is the first item.

171.title: ensure()
171.text:
The **ensure** method may be used to verify that all elements of a collection
are of a given type or list of types. Otherwise, an exception will be thrown.

172.title: mapWithKey()
172.text:
The **mapWithKey** method iterates through the collection with access to a related
collection, allowing transformation based on related data.
